record.original_question: (“runs” conjecture, due to Kolpakov and Kucherov, 1999): For a binary alphabet the number of runs is bounded by n.

evidence.quote: (“runs” conjecture, due to Kolpakov and Kucherov, 1999): For a binary alphabet the number of runs is bounded by n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ be a finite word of length $n$ over the binary alphabet $\{0,1\}$. A run (also called a maximal repetition) in $w$ is a triple $(i, j, p)$ such that the factor $w_i w_{i+1} \cdots w_j$ has smallest period $p$ with $j - i + 1 \ge 2p$, and this run is maximal in the sense that the period $p$ is broken upon extending the factor to the left (if $i > 1$) or to the right (if $j < n$). Let $\rho(n)$ denote the maximum, taken over all binary words $w$ of length $n$, of the number of runs occurring in $w$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$,
$$\rho(n) < n.$$
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / runs in strings
artifact.status_search_result: The runs conjecture of Kolpakov and Kucherov (1999) was proved by Bannai, I, Inenaga, Nakashima, Takeda, and Tsuruta in "The 'Runs' Theorem" (arXiv:1406.0263, published in SIAM J. Comput. 2017), establishing that the number of runs in any string of length n is less than n. The proof uses a Lyndon-word based characterization of runs and applies to general (in particular binary) alphabets.

status_evidence.title: The "Runs" Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: New characterization of maximal repetitions (runs) based on Lyndon words leads to a proof that the number of runs in a string of length n is less than n.
status_evidence.claim: Bannai et al. proved the runs conjecture, showing ρ(n) < n.

status_evidence.title: The "Runs" Theorem — SIAM Journal on Computing
status_evidence.snippet: Published proof of the runs conjecture in SIAM J. Comput., 2017.
status_evidence.claim: The proof appeared in a peer-reviewed venue, confirming the conjecture is solved.
